newsitem.title: FRANCE: French voters find right a bit more credible - poll.
newsitem.headline: French voters find right a bit more credible - poll.

text.p: French voters find the main campaign promises of the centre-right government a bit more credible than those of the left ahead of France's snap parliamentary election, according to an IFOP poll published on Monday.

The survey for the French daily Liberation found, for example, that nearly six out of 10 voters found unrealistic the opposition Socialists' key promises to create 700,000 new jobs and reduce the working week to 35 hours from 39 should they win the two-stage vote on May 25 and June 1.
Just half of voters, on the other hand, said they found implausible the centre-right's promises to shift to a single European currency from 1999 and to reduce state spending enough to cut taxes.

A majority of voters accepted as realistic centre-right pledges to lower payroll taxes for low-paid workers, limit the size of the cabinet to at most 15 ministers and train all students to use the Internet global computer network.

Similarly, a majority of voters found plausible Socialist promises to lower the value-added tax on some basic necessities, limit all politicians' terms to five years, raise taxes on the wealthy and renegotiate the terms for the switchover to European monetary union.
The survey of 1,000 registered voters was conducted on Saturday.
